guide.name: Southern Appalachian Fall Color from Brasstown Bald to Grayson Highlands
guide.description: Leaf-season drives, overlooks and short hikes across north Georgia, the Highlands-Cashiers plateau, the Cherohala Skyway, Roan Mountain and southwest Virginia, with a few places to stay and eat.
guide.region: Georgia, North Carolina, Tennessee and Virginia

sections.name: Amicalola Falls to Cloudland Canyon, Georgia
Cherohala Skyway, Tennessee and North Carolina

properties.name: Brasstown Bald
properties.notes: Georgia's highest point, with an observation deck that looks out over four states. Walk the steep paved trail from the parking lot or take the seasonal shuttle. The Forest Service charges a day-use fee; check its site for current hours.

properties.name: Vogel State Park
properties.notes: One of Georgia's oldest state parks, set at the foot of Blood Mountain with cabins, campsites and trails through hardwood coves. The drive in on US 129 through Neels Gap is part of the point. Lake Trahlyta has been drained for dam repairs; check the official site.
properties.address: 405 Vogel State Park Rd, Blairsville, GA 30512

properties.name: Brasstown Valley Resort & Spa
properties.notes: A big lodge-style resort in an open valley a short drive from Brasstown Bald, with rooms, cottages, a spa and walking trails on the grounds. A comfortable base for the Georgia high country.

properties.name: Black Rock Mountain State Park
properties.notes: Georgia's highest state park sits right on the Eastern Continental Divide. Overlooks near the summit look east over Rabun County, and the Tennessee Rock loop is a short, steady climb with wide views.
properties.address: 3085 Black Rock Mountain Pkwy, Mountain City, GA 30562

properties.name: The Dillard House
properties.notes: A family-run dining room that has served Southern meals family style for more than a century. Bowls of fried chicken, country ham and vegetables come to the table until you say stop. Reservations help on leaf weekends.

properties.name: Tallulah Gorge State Park
properties.notes: A two-mile-long gorge nearly a thousand feet deep, with rim trails, overlooks and a suspension bridge over the river. Gorge-floor permits are free but limited each day and not issued on water-release weekends; check the official site.
properties.address: 338 Jane Hurt Yarn Dr, Tallulah Falls, GA 30573

properties.name: Amicalola Falls State Park
properties.notes: A tall cascade with a long staircase beside it and color on every side. The approach trail to Springer Mountain and the start of the Appalachian Trail begins here. Parking fees apply.
properties.address: 166 Amicalola Falls State Park Rd, Dawsonville, GA 30534

properties.name: Amicalola Falls Lodge
properties.notes: The state park lodge sits on the ridge above the falls, with big windows facing the foothills. A mid-priced stay with trails from the door.
properties.address: 418 Amicalola Falls Lodge Road, Dawsonville, GA 30534

properties.name: Fort Mountain State Park
properties.notes: A mountaintop park on the western edge of the Cohuttas, with an old stone wall of debated origin and a stone fire tower built by the Civilian Conservation Corps. Overlooks face west across the valley, so late afternoon light is best.
properties.address: 181 Fort Mountain Park Rd, Chatsworth, GA 30705

properties.name: Cloudland Canyon State Park
properties.notes: A deep sandstone canyon on Lookout Mountain, with an easy rim walk to the main overlook and a stair-heavy trail down to two waterfalls. Color often peaks a little later here than in the higher mountains.
properties.address: 122 Cloudland Canyon Park Rd, Rising Fawn, GA 30738

properties.name: Whiteside Mountain Trail
properties.notes: A two-mile loop along the top of sheer granite cliffs, looking down on the Chattooga valley. Go early on October weekends, when the small lot fills fast. There is a parking fee.

properties.name: Sunset Rock
properties.notes: A short walk from the edge of town to a granite outcrop that looks straight down on Highlands and across to Whiteside. As the name says, come at the end of the day.
properties.address: Ravenel Park, Horse Cove Rd, Highlands, NC 28741

properties.name: Dry Falls
properties.notes: A short path and stairs lead behind a waterfall in the Cullasaja Gorge. The drive west on US 64 through the gorge is narrow and slow but one of the prettiest in the region. Check the Forest Service site for closures.

properties.name: Whitewater Falls
properties.notes: One of the highest waterfalls in the East, seen from a paved path and a longer stairway down to a lower overlook. The surrounding gorge is thick with hardwoods. Check the Forest Service site for closures.

properties.name: High Hampton
properties.notes: A long-running mountain inn on a lake below Chimney Top, with an old chestnut-bark main lodge and cottages. A splurge, and a classic Cashiers place to wait out the color.

properties.name: Tellico Grains Bakery
properties.notes: A wood-fired bakery near the square in Tellico Plains, good for bread, pastries and sandwiches to take up the skyway. Stop on the way in, since there is little food along the road.

properties.name: Cherohala Skyway Visitor Center
properties.notes: The start of the skyway, a high, lightly traveled road that climbs over 5,000 feet on its way to Robbinsville. Pick up a map and fill the tank here; there are no services for over 40 miles.

properties.name: Bald River Falls
properties.notes: A broad waterfall you can see from the bridge on Tellico River Road, a short detour off the skyway. The river road itself is lined with color in late October.
properties.address: Tellico River Rd, Tellico Plains, TN 37385

properties.name: Huckleberry Knob
properties.notes: A grassy bald reached by an old road from the skyway, about a mile each way. From the top the ridges roll off in every direction, and the walk is easier than the view suggests.

properties.name: Joyce Kilmer Memorial Forest
properties.notes: A two-mile figure-eight loop through one of the largest stands of old-growth forest in the East, just below the skyway's eastern end. The giant poplars turn gold in fall. Mapping apps can misroute, so follow the Forest Service directions.

properties.name: Roan Mountain State Park
properties.notes: A valley park along the Doe River with cabins, a campground and trails through hardwood coves. A budget-friendly base for the Roan Highlands. Check the official site for any trail or cabin closures.

properties.name: Carvers Gap
properties.notes: Where the Appalachian Trail crosses the state line on the Roan. Head north up Round Bald and Jane Bald for open grassy summits. Color comes earlier at this elevation, so plan it for the start of the season.
properties.address: TN-143 at NC-261, Roan Mountain, TN 37687

properties.name: Grayson Highlands State Park
properties.notes: High, rocky meadows beside Mount Rogers, with wild ponies grazing among the boulders and blueberry bushes that turn deep red in fall. The park closes on a few fall days for resource management; check the official site.
properties.address: 829 Grayson Highland Ln, Mouth of Wilson, VA 24363

properties.name: Massie Gap
properties.notes: The main trailhead in the park, where the Rhododendron Trail climbs to the Appalachian Trail and the pony meadows. Even a short walk up from the lot gets you above the trees.
properties.address: 829 Grayson Highland Ln, Mouth of Wilson, VA 24363

properties.name: The Martha Washington Inn & Spa
properties.notes: An 1832 brick mansion turned hotel on Abingdon's main street, across from the Barter Theatre. Rocking chairs on the front porch and an easy drive to Grayson Highlands and Mount Rogers.
